newsitem.title: UK: Croatia firmer, rest of Brady market unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Croatia firmer, rest of Brady market unchanged.

text.p: The emerging debt market slumped into torpor on Wednesday with few expecting any more sparks this year.
One of the few highlights in the market has been the continuing strength of Croatian debt, based on expectations of an imminent credit rating for the country.
Croatia A loans were trading at 96-1/2 cents in the dollar in the morning, about 1/2 a point up from Tuesday. The price compares to around 88 cents three months ago.
"It will get investment grade. The question is which one," a U.S. bank trader said.
The market in general though is extremely quiet with hardly any trades during the morning.
There was no impact from the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates alone.

However, Bank of America analyst Richard Gray, noting the market was still guessing when the next rate hike would be, said investor strategy should be to keep exposure to improving country credits while insulating themselves from Fed moves.
"Buy uncollaterallised floaters, with high running yield, against fixed at least until there is evidence of a weaking U.S. economy," he said.
